ai-assistant.task: specify metrics precisely so the numbers on the dashboard mean the same to everyone
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Write precise definitions for these metrics, including the denominator and edge cases: [list].

coding-assistant.task: write the queries and chart components, and test them against known totals
coding-assistant.starterPrompt: Write a query that returns [measure] by week from these tables, and a test to check it against a known total: [schema].

framework.task: build the dashboard pages with server-side data loading and typed charts
framework.starterPrompt: Show how to load data on the server and render charts in a [framework] page, with loading and error states.

database.task: store raw and aggregated data so queries stay fast
database.starterPrompt: Design tables for raw events and a daily summary for a dashboard of [data]. What would I index?

authentication.task: restrict who can see which data in the dashboard
authentication.starterPrompt: How should I handle roles in a dashboard where each team sees only its own data?

data-analysis.task: validate metrics and examine segments before they go on screen
data-analysis.starterPrompt: Which checks should I run on this dataset before trusting its dashboard: duplicates, nulls, time zones and outliers?

hosting.task: deploy the dashboard with caching so it loads quickly for many viewers
hosting.starterPrompt: How should I cache dashboard queries so charts load fast but are never more than [time] old?

title: Automate repetitive tasks
headline: Your automation plan
example: I want to automate repetitive tasks at work
starterBrief:
Goal: automate [task] that I do [how often].
The steps today: [list].
The apps involved: [list].
What could go wrong if it makes a mistake: [risk].
Rule: start with a version that asks me to approve before it acts.
Ask me anything you need, then list the trigger, steps and checks.

simple.summary: Write the steps by hand first. Then connect two apps with a no-code tool, and let it ask for your approval at the end.
simple.goodFor: Workers who want one repetitive task to run itself without code.

steps.title: Write the steps
steps.detail: List what you do, in order, every time. If you cannot list it, you cannot automate it.

steps.title: Pick the trigger
steps.detail: Choose the event that starts it: a new row, a new email, a time.

steps.title: Build it in {job:automation-and-workflows}
steps.detail: Connect the two apps and run it on one real example.

steps.title: Add an approval
steps.detail: Make it send you a draft first, not act on its own.

commonMistakes: Automating a task you do not understand.
Letting it act without approval at first.
Sharing access to apps with too many permissions.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check what data passes through each connected app, and what each app is allowed to do.

ai-assistant.task: break one repetitive task into steps and spot which ones a tool can do
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here is a task I repeat each week: [describe]. List the steps, mark which can be automated and what could go wrong.

automation-and-workflows.task: connect two apps so one action starts the next step without you
automation-and-workflows.starterPrompt: Walk me through building an automation that, when [trigger], does [action]. Include how to test it with one example.

polished.summary: Add AI steps for sorting and drafting, error alerts and a log of what ran.
polished.goodFor: Workers who want several apps linked, with a spreadsheet and email in the loop.

steps.title: Add a drafting step
steps.detail: Let {job:ai-assistant} draft replies or summaries, and keep a human check.

steps.title: Log everything
steps.detail: Write each run to a sheet with {job:spreadsheet-ai}.

steps.title: Alert on failure
steps.detail: Get a message when a step fails.

steps.title: Review weekly
steps.detail: Read ten runs a week for the first month.

commonMistakes: Sending AI drafts without a review.
polished.checkTheFacts: Never send customer-facing messages without a person reading them first.

ai-assistant.task: write the rules and the message text the automation will use
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Write the rules for sorting these incoming messages into three categories, with a sample reply for each: [describe].

automation-and-workflows.task: chain several steps, add conditions and be told when something fails
automation-and-workflows.starterPrompt: Design a workflow with a trigger, a condition and two actions, and describe how I get an alert if it fails.

spreadsheet-ai.task: log each run in a sheet so you can see what happened and fix mistakes
spreadsheet-ai.starterPrompt: What columns should an automation log sheet have so I can audit each run?

email-writing.task: draft the standard replies and notifications the workflow sends
email-writing.starterPrompt: Write a short standard reply for [situation] that I can send automatically, plus one variation for urgent cases.

advanced.summary: Write custom scripts for what no-code tools cannot do, in version control, with tests and secrets stored safely.
advanced.goodFor: Developers who want custom, versioned automation with storage and a host.

steps.title: Write the script
steps.detail: Ask {job:coding-assistant} for a script that does one step.

steps.title: Keep secrets out of code
steps.detail: Store keys in environment settings, never in the repository.

steps.title: Schedule and host
steps.detail: Run it with {job:hosting} or a scheduler.

steps.title: Test with bad input
steps.detail: Feed it empty and broken data and see what it does.

No way to stop it quickly.
advanced.checkTheFacts: A script that acts on real accounts needs a way to stop it and a record of what it did.

ai-assistant.task: document the process, edge cases and what must stay a human decision
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Document this automation: what triggers it, what it changes, where it can fail and who is told: [paste description].

coding-assistant.task: write scripts for steps no ready connector handles and test them
coding-assistant.starterPrompt: Write a script that [does task], with error handling and a dry-run mode, in [language].

automation-and-workflows.task: orchestrate multiple systems with retries, schedules and shared secrets
automation-and-workflows.starterPrompt: Design a workflow with retries and a dead-letter step so failed runs are not lost.

version-control.task: keep scripts and workflow exports in history so changes can be reviewed and reverted
version-control.starterPrompt: Which parts of an automation setup should live in version control, and what should stay out?

database.task: keep state between runs so the workflow never processes the same item twice
database.starterPrompt: Design a small table to track processed items so an automation is idempotent.

hosting.task: run scheduled jobs on a server you control, with logs you can read
hosting.starterPrompt: How do I run a scheduled script on a small server with logs and failure alerts?

simple.summary: Choose a narrow topic, plan ten videos and make the first one with what you already have. Improve from the second.

steps.title: Pick a narrow topic
steps.detail: Write one sentence: who the channel is for and what they get.

steps.title: Plan ten videos

steps.title: Record simply
steps.detail: Record with your phone in a quiet room. Clear sound matters more than a fancy camera.

steps.title: Edit and upload
steps.detail: Cut the pauses in {job:video-editing} and upload with a plain title.

steps.title: Research titles
steps.detail: Use {job:seo} to see what viewers search for before you title.

steps.title: Review each upload
steps.detail: Check which videos viewers leave early, and change the next hook.

seo.starterPrompt: Write three title options and a 100-word description for a video about [topic], with natural search words.

voice-and-audio.starterPrompt: Plan how to dub my videos into [language]: workflow, quality checks and how to label the audio tracks.

design-tool.task: keep channel art, thumbnails and end screens in one consistent kit
design-tool.starterPrompt: List the assets a channel kit needs (banner, thumbnails, end screens) and the rules that keep them consistent.

seo.task: plan topics around search demand and test titles against click-through
seo.starterPrompt: Suggest a content plan of ten videos around search demand for [topic], with how to test two titles each.

music-generation.task: make royalty-safe background tracks that fit your series mood

social-media.starterPrompt: Turn this video outline into three short clips with a hook and a caption for each: [paste outline].

steps.title: Gather directions
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for naming and style directions.
steps.examplePrompt: Give me three brand directions for [business] that feel [three words]: colours, font style and a logo idea for each. Do not suggest existing brand names.

steps.title: Make it in {job:design-tool}
steps.detail: Try three simple marks. Prefer one shape and one or two colours.

steps.title: Test small and in black and white
steps.detail: Check it works as a tiny icon and without colour.

commonMistakes: Too much detail that disappears when small.
Not checking whether the name is taken.
whenToUpgrade: You want cards, posters and a kit.
You want a website that matches.
simple.checkTheFacts: Search the name and logo on the web and in the trademark register of your country before you commit.

ai-assistant.task: define what the brand stands for and shortlist names, colours and a tone of voice
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: My business is [description] for [audience]. Suggest five brand adjectives, a colour direction and a tagline in three tones.

design-tool.task: draw a simple logo with one typeface and two colours that works small
design-tool.starterPrompt: Describe three simple logo concepts for [business], each using only text and one shape.

stock-assets.task: pick a licensed typeface and icons that suit the brand
stock-assets.starterPrompt: Suggest font pairings for a [type] brand that are free to use for business, and how to use them.

polished.summary: Build a small kit: logo variants, two fonts, a colour set and templates for the things you use most.
polished.goodFor: Businesses that want a fuller kit with assets and a small website.

steps.title: Make logo variants
steps.detail: Create a horizontal, stacked and icon-only version.

steps.title: Fix the palette
steps.detail: Choose a main colour, a dark and a light, and check readability.

steps.title: Make templates
steps.detail: Build social, card and poster templates in {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Write the rules
steps.detail: Write half a page: how to use the logo, spacing and colours.

polished.checkTheFacts: AI-generated marks can resemble existing ones. Check for similarity before use.

ai-assistant.task: write the brand guide: voice, colours, logo use and what not to do
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Write a one-page brand guide for [business]: voice, colour roles, logo clear space and three do and don't rules.

design-tool.task: refine the logo and produce variants for light, dark and small sizes
design-tool.starterPrompt: List the logo variants I need (full, icon, one-colour) and the sizes to export each at.

stock-assets.task: collect licensed icons, patterns and photos in the brand style
stock-assets.starterPrompt: What should I look for in brand photography and icons so they match my logo and colours?

image-generation.task: explore mood and pattern ideas before choosing a visual direction
image-generation.starterPrompt: Write an image prompt for a brand mood board for [business] in [style], using the palette [colours].

ui-templates.task: apply the brand to a ready website layout in an hour
ui-templates.starterPrompt: Which website sections should carry the brand most strongly, and how should the logo appear in the header?

advanced.summary: Make a full system: guidelines, accessible colour pairs, templates and files ready for print and web.
advanced.goodFor: Brands that want custom visuals, 3D marks and consistent web and social use.

steps.title: Check accessibility
steps.detail: Test every text and background pair for contrast.

steps.title: Prepare print files
steps.detail: Export vector and print-ready files with proper margins.

steps.title: Build a design system
steps.detail: Create buttons, cards and headings in {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Document
steps.detail: Write the rules and keep source files together.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Seek legal advice for trademark questions.

ai-assistant.task: stress-test the positioning and keep naming, tone and claims consistent across channels
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here is our positioning: [paste]. Point out claims that are vague and wording that conflicts with our brand voice.

design-tool.task: build a full identity system with grids, templates and component kits
design-tool.starterPrompt: Outline an identity system for [business]: logo set, colour roles, type scale, layout grid and templates.

image-generation.task: generate a coherent illustration and texture language for the brand
image-generation.starterPrompt: Write prompts for four brand illustrations in the same style, to be used on a website and social posts: [themes].

stock-assets.task: assemble licensed typefaces, icons and photography that stay consistent
stock-assets.starterPrompt: Create a checklist to review licences for fonts, icons and images in a brand kit.

3d-and-design-assets.task: build a 3D version of the mark or product mock-ups for packaging and web
3d-and-design-assets.starterPrompt: What do I need to turn a flat logo into a clean 3D mark that I can reuse in renders and animation?

ui-templates.task: apply the identity to web templates so pages match the brand system
ui-templates.starterPrompt: Review this page layout against our brand rules and list where it breaks them: [describe].

title: UI design
headline: Your UI design plan
example: I want to design the screens of an app in Figma
starterBrief:
Goal: UI designs for [product] used by [people] to [task].
Screens needed: [list].
Platform: [web, phone].
Existing brand: [colours, fonts, none].
Rule: design for the main task first, then check accessibility.
Ask me anything you need, then list the screens and flows.

simple.summary: Sketch the main flow as boxes, then build three screens from a ready-made kit. Click through it yourself.
simple.goodFor: Beginners designing a first set of app screens.

steps.title: Write the task
steps.detail: State what the person is trying to do in one sentence.

steps.title: Sketch the flow
steps.detail: Draw three to five boxes: start, the main action, done.

steps.title: Build from a kit
steps.detail: Use {job:ui-templates} or a kit in {job:design-tool} and change text only.

steps.title: Click through
steps.detail: Link the screens into a prototype and walk through it as a new user.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my flow: [list]. What would confuse a first-time user at each step?

commonMistakes: Designing every screen before the main flow.
whenToUpgrade: You want to test with users.
You want to hand it to developers.
simple.checkTheFacts: Test colour contrast and tap sizes before you call a design done.

ai-assistant.task: list the screens and the main user flow before drawing anything
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: List the screens and the main flow for an app that [idea], from opening to the key action, with what is on each screen.

design-tool.task: lay out each screen with a simple grid and reusable buttons
design-tool.starterPrompt: Give me a layout for a mobile home screen of an app that [idea]: header, main content and bottom navigation.

ui-templates.task: start from a ready screen kit and adapt it to your content and colours
ui-templates.starterPrompt: Which templates or screen kits suit an app that [idea]? List the screen types I should look for.

polished.summary: Build a small design system and test with five people, then fix what they struggle with.
polished.goodFor: Designers who want consistent assets, flows and starting layouts.

steps.title: Map the flows
steps.detail: Draw them in {job:diagramming}.

steps.title: Create the system
steps.detail: Colour, type, spacing, buttons and inputs, as components in {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Design states
steps.detail: Show hover, focus, empty, loading and error.

steps.title: Test with five people
steps.detail: Give each one a task and note where they hesitate.

whenToUpgrade: You need to scale across products.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check accessibility: contrast, text size, focus order and touch targets.

ai-assistant.task: write the interface text and review the flow for dead ends
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Review this user flow for dead ends and unclear steps, and rewrite the button labels in plain words: [paste].

design-tool.task: build consistent components with states for hover, focus and error
design-tool.starterPrompt: List the states each button, input and card in my design needs, and how to show each clearly.

stock-assets.task: use one icon set and one image style throughout the screens
stock-assets.starterPrompt: How do I choose one icon style and keep it consistent across all my screens?

diagramming.task: map the user journey and the screens that connect with arrows
diagramming.starterPrompt: Map the user journey for [task] as a flow with decisions and what the screen shows at each step.

ui-templates.task: use a layout kit for the standard screens and spend time on the unique ones
ui-templates.starterPrompt: Which screens in an app that [idea] are standard enough to start from a template?

advanced.summary: Hand off cleanly: tokens, specs, motion and code for the interface, with accessibility checked.
advanced.goodFor: Designers who work with a shared component system and hand off code.

steps.title: Define tokens
steps.detail: List colours, spacing and type as named values.

steps.title: Match components
steps.detail: Map each design component to {job:component-library}.

steps.title: Specify motion
steps.detail: Describe animation with {job:animation-library} and keep it optional.

steps.title: Review the build
steps.detail: Compare the live screens with the design.

commonMistakes: Animation that cannot be turned off.
No review of the built version.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check against accessibility standards, not only visual taste.

ai-assistant.task: write design rationale, accessibility notes and handoff documentation
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Write handoff notes for this screen: states, spacing rules, accessibility needs and edge cases: [describe].

design-tool.task: organise tokens, variants and auto layout into a shared design system
design-tool.starterPrompt: Outline a token set for colours, spacing and type for a design system, and how components should reference them.

component-library.task: match the design components to coded ones so handoff is a one-to-one
component-library.starterPrompt: Map these design components to a coded component library and flag the ones that have no equivalent: [list].

animation-library.task: specify motion that explains changes without slowing the interface
animation-library.starterPrompt: Specify transitions for opening a dialog and switching tabs, with durations and a reduced-motion alternative.

coding-assistant.task: turn the design into working front-end code and check it matches
coding-assistant.starterPrompt: Convert this design spec into an accessible component with the states listed: [paste spec].

stock-assets.task: keep icon, illustration and font licences tidy across the whole system
stock-assets.starterPrompt: List the licence details I should record for each asset in a design system.

title: Research paper
headline: Your research paper plan
example: I need to write a research paper with proper citations
starterBrief:
Goal: a research paper on [topic] for [course or journal].
Length and format: [words, citation style].
My sources so far: [list].
My own contribution or argument: [one sentence].
Rule: do not invent sources, quotes or numbers. Use only what I give you.
Ask me anything you need, then give me an outline.

simple.summary: Find real sources first, then outline, then write each section yourself. Use AI to organise, not to invent.
simple.goodFor: Students writing a first paper with a few sources and a clear outline.

steps.title: Fix the question
steps.detail: Write the one question the paper answers.

steps.title: Find real sources
steps.detail: Use {job:research-with-sources} and open every source you cite.

steps.title: Outline
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to structure the sections around your question.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my question and my sources: [list]. Suggest an outline with the argument for each section. Do not add sources I did not list.

steps.title: Write and edit
steps.detail: Write each section yourself, then use {job:writing-and-editing} for grammar.

commonMistakes: Citing a paper you did not open.
whenToUpgrade: You have many papers to read.
You need to submit to a journal.
simple.checkTheFacts: Open every reference and confirm it exists and says what you claim. Generated citations are often invented.

ai-assistant.task: narrow the topic into a research question and an outline with a thesis
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: My paper topic is [topic] for [course]. Suggest three narrower research questions and an outline for the best one.

research-with-sources.task: find credible papers on the question and note where each claim comes from
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: Find peer-reviewed papers on [question] and give a one-line summary of each, with a link.

writing-and-editing.task: check your draft for clarity, grammar and passive phrasing before you submit
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Edit this paragraph of my paper for clarity and academic tone without changing my argument: [paste].

polished.summary: Read papers faster with document chat, track notes by source and add charts for your own data.
polished.goodFor: Students working from many papers who need notes and sourced claims.

steps.title: Triage papers
steps.detail: Ask {job:pdf-and-document-chat} what each paper claims, then read the important ones yourself.

steps.title: Keep source notes
steps.detail: Write each claim and its page in {job:note-taking}.

steps.title: Draft
steps.detail: Write from your notes, citing as you go.

steps.title: Run the checks
steps.detail: Use {job:writing-and-editing} to check grammar and plagiarism.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my paragraph and the source: [text]. Is any part too close to the source wording?

commonMistakes: Trusting a summary of a paper you did not read.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check quotes and numbers against the original paper, not the summary.

ai-assistant.task: stress-test your argument and find the weakest paragraph
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here is my argument: [paste]. List the three strongest objections a reviewer would raise and where my evidence is thin.

research-with-sources.task: map the literature, with who cites whom, so your review is not just a list
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: Group the papers on [topic] by their main position and note the key disagreement between groups.

pdf-and-document-chat.task: ask questions of a paper and get answers pointing to the section they come from
pdf-and-document-chat.starterPrompt: From this paper, extract the method, sample size and main finding, and say which section each came from.

note-taking.task: keep one note per paper with quotes, page numbers and your own comments
note-taking.starterPrompt: Create a literature note template: reference, question, method, finding, limitation and relevance to my paper.

writing-and-editing.task: tighten sentences and keep a consistent academic voice from section to section
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Review this section for repetition and vague claims, and flag any claim without a citation: [paste].

advanced.summary: Add your own analysis, figures and a careful review pass before you submit.
advanced.goodFor: Authors who analyse data, map arguments and need every claim traceable.

steps.title: Analyse your data
steps.detail: Use {job:data-analysis} and record each step so it can be repeated.

steps.title: Make figures
steps.detail: Draw diagrams with {job:diagramming} and label every axis.

steps.title: Stress-test the argument
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to find weak points.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my argument and evidence: [text]. List the three strongest objections and what evidence would answer them.

steps.title: Submit carefully
steps.detail: Follow the venue's format and disclosure rules for AI help.

commonMistakes: Changing the analysis after seeing the result without saying so.
Hiding AI use where disclosure is required.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check each venue's policy on AI-assisted writing and disclose use if required.

ai-assistant.task: plan the structure of the whole paper and keep claims consistent across sections
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here are my section summaries: [paste]. Check that the abstract, results and conclusion claim the same thing.

research-with-sources.task: verify each claim against a source you have opened before it goes in the paper
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: For each claim in my draft, list a source that supports it, or mark it as unsupported: [paste claims].

pdf-and-document-chat.task: compare methods and results across a whole folder of papers
pdf-and-document-chat.starterPrompt: Across these papers, build a table of method, sample, result and limitation, with page references.

data-analysis.task: run and check the analysis behind your results and produce clean figures
data-analysis.starterPrompt: Suggest the right statistical test for [question] with this data, and the assumptions I must check: [describe data].

note-taking.task: link evidence to the claim it supports so the argument can be audited
note-taking.starterPrompt: Design a claim and evidence table that links each claim in my paper to its source and strength.

writing-and-editing.task: do a final pass for style, consistency and reference formatting
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Check these references for consistent formatting in [style] and list any that are incomplete: [paste].

diagramming.task: draw the argument structure and the study design as figures
diagramming.starterPrompt: Describe a diagram of my study design with participants, steps and outcomes for a figure in the methods section.

title: Thesis or dissertation
headline: Your thesis plan
example: I need to write my thesis and manage references
starterBrief:
Goal: finish my [thesis, project report] on [topic] by [date].
Word count and format: [numbers, style guide].
What is done: [chapters].
My supervisor wants: [notes].
Rule: do not invent data, results or references.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a weekly plan.

simple.summary: Break it into chapters with dates, and write a little every day. Use AI for planning and checking structure only.
simple.goodFor: Students starting out who need a structure and a place for notes.

steps.title: List the chapters
steps.detail: Write chapter titles with a one-line purpose for each, and a date.

steps.title: Plan the week
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to turn the dates into a weekly plan.
steps.examplePrompt: My thesis has these chapters and deadlines: [list]. Make a realistic weekly writing plan with buffer days.

steps.title: Write daily
steps.detail: Write 300 words a day in your own words in {job:note-taking} or your editor.

steps.title: Edit in passes
steps.detail: Use {job:writing-and-editing} for grammar after content is final.

whenToUpgrade: You need formatting for the university.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check your university's rules about AI assistance and originality before using any tool.

ai-assistant.task: break the thesis into chapters and a weekly writing plan you can keep to
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: My thesis is on [topic] and is due on [date]. Propose a chapter outline and a weekly plan with milestones.

writing-and-editing.task: keep the prose clear and consistent as chapters grow
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Check this thesis paragraph for clarity and consistent terminology: [paste].

note-taking.task: collect reading notes by chapter so you can find them while you write
note-taking.starterPrompt: Suggest a folder and note structure for a thesis with one note per source and one per chapter.

polished.summary: Manage references and papers properly, and keep notes so each chapter is built from evidence.
polished.goodFor: Students managing many references who want sourced answers from their reading.

steps.title: Build the reference list
steps.detail: Use {job:research-with-sources} and keep every source in one list.

steps.title: Read efficiently
steps.detail: Use {job:pdf-and-document-chat} to find where a claim is, then read it.

steps.title: Link notes to chapters
steps.detail: Tag notes by chapter in {job:note-taking}.

steps.title: Check consistency
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to list terms used differently across chapters.

commonMistakes: Not saving the page for a quote.
whenToUpgrade: You are close to the deadline.
polished.checkTheFacts: Verify every reference exists and supports your claim.

ai-assistant.task: plan each chapter's argument and check it ties back to your research question
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here is my research question and chapter plan: [paste]. Tell me if any chapter does not contribute to answering the question.

research-with-sources.task: find the key papers in each subtopic and keep their references organised
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: List the key papers on [subtopic] and who disagrees with whom, with a source link for each.

pdf-and-document-chat.task: ask your whole reading list questions and get answers with page numbers
pdf-and-document-chat.starterPrompt: Using only these papers, how do authors define [concept]? Quote the passage and give the page.

note-taking.task: link notes to chapters and keep quotes with their references
note-taking.starterPrompt: Create a note template for a thesis source: reference, key claim, quote with page and how I will use it.

writing-and-editing.task: edit chapters for tone and flow without losing your own voice
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Edit this chapter introduction to be more direct. Keep my terminology and my argument: [paste].

advanced.summary: Add analysis, figures and a defence plan, with a clean final check of format and references.
advanced.goodFor: Students who analyse data, map arguments and prepare a defence deck.

steps.title: Document the analysis
steps.detail: Record every step in {job:data-analysis}.

steps.title: Check figures
steps.detail: Number and caption each figure from {job:diagramming}.

steps.title: Prepare the defence
steps.detail: Build slides in {job:presentation-maker} and ask {job:ai-assistant} for tough questions.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my thesis summary: [text]. List ten hard questions an examiner might ask and where my evidence is weakest.

steps.title: Final check
steps.detail: Check the format, citations and list of figures.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Numbers in text, tables and figures must agree. Check each one.

ai-assistant.task: prepare for tough questions by role-playing the examiner on your own chapters
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Act as a thesis examiner. Ask me one hard question about my methodology at a time and critique my answers.

research-with-sources.task: verify claims against your sources before your examiner does
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: Check each of these claims against my sources and flag any that the source does not support: [paste].

data-analysis.task: analyse results and produce figures with the right test for your design
data-analysis.starterPrompt: Which analysis fits my design with [groups and measures]? List assumptions to test and how to report the results.

diagramming.task: draw the conceptual framework and the study design as clear figures
diagramming.starterPrompt: Describe a figure of my conceptual framework with the variables and the relationships I expect.

writing-and-editing.task: final-pass the thesis for consistency, abbreviations and reference style
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Check that terms and abbreviations are defined once and used consistently across this chapter: [paste].

presentation-maker.task: turn the thesis into a defence deck that tells the story in twenty minutes
presentation-maker.starterPrompt: Outline a 20-minute thesis defence deck: question, method, findings, limits and what comes next.

title: Essay writing
headline: Your essay plan
example: I need to write an essay for my class
starterBrief:
Goal: an essay on [topic] of [length] for [class, level].
My position or main point: [one sentence].
What I must include: [instructions].
Rule: use my own words and my facts; do not invent quotes or numbers.
Ask me anything you need, then help me outline before I write.

simple.summary: Decide your point, outline, write a rough draft yourself and then fix it. Use AI to ask questions and check.
simple.goodFor: Students who want to improve their own draft, not have one written for them.

steps.title: Write your point
steps.detail: State your main point in one sentence.

steps.title: Outline
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to question your point and suggest an order.
steps.examplePrompt: My essay point is: [point]. Ask me five questions that would strengthen it, then suggest a four-part outline.

steps.title: Write the draft
steps.detail: Write it in your own words, without stopping to fix.

steps.title: Edit
steps.detail: Use {job:writing-and-editing} for grammar and clarity, and read it aloud once.

commonMistakes: Pasting AI text as your own.
simple.checkTheFacts: Submit only work that follows your school's rules about AI help, and check any facts you use.

ai-assistant.task: shape the question into a thesis and an outline, then give feedback on your draft
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: My essay question is [question]. Help me form a thesis and a four-part outline. I will write the essay myself.

writing-and-editing.task: fix grammar and awkward sentences while your voice stays yours
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Point out grammar errors and unclear sentences in this paragraph and explain each fix: [paste].

polished.summary: Add real sources, a tighter argument and an originality check.
polished.goodFor: Students who want sources and tidy notes behind a stronger argument.

steps.title: Find sources
steps.detail: Use {job:research-with-sources} and open every source you cite.

steps.title: Take notes
steps.detail: Write each fact with its source in {job:note-taking}.

steps.title: Strengthen the argument
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for the strongest counterpoint and answer it.

steps.title: Edit and check
steps.detail: Use {job:writing-and-editing} to proofread and check originality.

commonMistakes: Changing a few words and calling it your own.
whenToUpgrade: You are applying to a programme.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check quotes and numbers against the original source.

ai-assistant.task: challenge your argument and show where a reader would ask for evidence
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here is my thesis and main points: [paste]. Where would a sceptical teacher ask for evidence?

writing-and-editing.task: edit for structure, transitions and a clear first sentence for each paragraph
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Check whether each paragraph of my essay starts with its main point and flows to the next: [paste].

research-with-sources.task: find reliable sources and quotes you can cite properly
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: Find three reliable sources on [topic] I can cite, with a link and one line on how each supports an argument.

note-taking.task: keep quotes with their sources so referencing is quick
note-taking.starterPrompt: What should I note down for each source I use in an essay so I can cite it later without searching again?

advanced.summary: Treat it as research: weigh sources, structure a real argument and revise in passes.
advanced.goodFor: Students writing a long essay from many readings who need every point traced.

steps.title: Read for the argument
steps.detail: Use {job:pdf-and-document-chat} to locate the key claims, then read those parts.

steps.title: Map the debate
steps.detail: List who disagrees and why in {job:note-taking}.

steps.title: Draft and revise
steps.detail: Revise for argument first, then style.

steps.title: Final check
steps.detail: Check citation style and every reference.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Check that every claim is supported by a source you read.

ai-assistant.task: map your readings to the argument and spot where two sources contradict
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: Here are notes on my sources: [paste]. Map which source supports which point and where they contradict.

research-with-sources.task: check that each claim is supported by a source you have actually read
research-with-sources.starterPrompt: List the claims in my essay that need a citation and suggest where the evidence may be found: [paste].

pdf-and-document-chat.task: pull exact passages from your readings with page numbers
pdf-and-document-chat.starterPrompt: Find the passages in this reading that discuss [concept], with page numbers and a quote for each.

note-taking.task: link quotes, claims and counter-arguments in one structure
note-taking.starterPrompt: Design a note layout that links each essay claim to its evidence and the strongest counterpoint.

writing-and-editing.task: do a last pass for style, citation format and word count
writing-and-editing.starterPrompt: Check this bibliography for consistent [style] formatting and missing details: [paste].

title: Exam preparation
headline: Your exam preparation plan
example: I need to prepare for my exams in two months
starterBrief:
Goal: be ready for [exam] on [date].
Subjects and weight: [list].
What I know well: [topics]. What I find hard: [topics].
Hours per day: [number].
Rule: build a realistic plan with revision and rest, and do not make up the syllabus.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a weekly timetable.

simple.summary: Write down the syllabus, set weekly goals and use short daily revision with practice questions.
simple.goodFor: Students who want a plan, organised notes and practice cards.

steps.title: List the syllabus
steps.detail: Copy it from the official source, and mark each topic as strong, ok or weak.

steps.title: Plan the weeks
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a timetable, then edit it to your real hours.
steps.examplePrompt: I have [days] until my exam and [hours] a day. Topics: [list with strong/weak]. Make a weekly plan with revision and one rest day.

steps.title: Make short notes
steps.detail: Write one page per topic in {job:note-taking}.

steps.title: Test yourself daily
steps.detail: Use {job:flashcards-and-quizzes} for ten minutes at the start of each day.

simple.checkTheFacts: Use the official syllabus and past papers, not a made-up list. Check any answer AI gives you.

ai-assistant.task: split the syllabus across the weeks left and mark the topics worth most marks
ai-assistant.starterPrompt: My exams are in [number] weeks and the topics are [list]. Make a weekly schedule with revision and practice tests.

note-taking.task: condense each topic into one revision page you can reread quickly
note-taking.starterPrompt: Turn these class notes into a one-page revision sheet with key terms, formulas and typical questions: [paste].

flashcards-and-quizzes.task: make cards for facts and definitions and review them every day
flashcards-and-quizzes.starterPrompt: Make 20 question-and-answer cards from this chapter, one fact per card: [paste].

polished.summary: Add doubt-clearing, mock tests under time and a revision cycle that repeats weak topics.
polished.goodFor: Students who need help on tough problems and a calendar that holds them to the plan.

steps.title: Clear doubts early
steps.detail: Use {job:study-help-and-math} for steps, then redo the problem yourself.

steps.title: Do timed mocks
steps.detail: Take a full mock weekly and review every mistake.

steps.title: Track mistakes

title: Plan built from your parts
headline: Your custom plan
example: A plan built from the parts I describe
starterBrief:
Goal: [what I want to achieve].
The parts I need: [list].
Who it is for: [audience].
What I already have: [tools, files, skills].
Rule: use only facts I give you, and say what you are unsure about.
Ask me anything you need, then give me the order to do the parts in.

simple.summary: Work through the parts in order: idea first, then design, build, data, payments, launch and growth. Do one part at a time and check it.
simple.goodFor: People who named the parts they need and want the simplest tool for each.

steps.title: Write the goal in one sentence
steps.detail: Say who it is for and what done looks like.

steps.title: Start with the idea
steps.detail: Use {job:ai-assistant} to turn your sentence into a short list of what must exist.

steps.title: Do the parts in order
steps.detail: Work down the cards. Finish one part before starting the next.

steps.title: Check each part
steps.detail: Test the part on a small real example before you move on.

commonMistakes: Paying for tools before you have tried the free options.
Trusting the first answer without checking.
whenToUpgrade: A part turns out bigger than expected.
Two parts need to work together.
You want a plan that matches a common goal.
simple.checkTheFacts: AI output can be wrong or invented. Check anything that matters against the original or a trusted source.

polished.summary: Add design and structure: decide how the parts connect, and write down the data that moves between them.
polished.goodFor: People who want each part covered with a tool that works well with the others.

steps.title: Draw how the parts connect
steps.detail: A box for each part and an arrow for what passes between them.

steps.title: Choose tools that work together
steps.detail: Prefer tools that list each other as compatible, and read each card's note.

steps.title: Build in small steps
steps.detail: Finish one part end to end before the next.

steps.title: Write it down
steps.detail: Keep a short note of what you chose and why.

commonMistakes: Tools that do not fit each other.
No notes, so you cannot repeat it.

You need others to use it.

polished.checkTheFacts: AI output can be wrong or invented. Check anything that matters against the original or a trusted source.
